description: A company premium (a PREM- line from an employee-scoped pay policy with a worked-time rule) is taxed at year end exactly as the cutoff taxed it. The cutoff withholds on a premium whose rule says taxable: false as if it were not paid, and on a taxable one as ordinary pay. Year-end annualization must do the same: a PREM- line whose notes say 'Taxable: no' joins the non-taxable bucket (otherNonTaxable). Phase 28 certifies it through the real engine with three workers hired at the switch on the same salary, each with the same complete 8-hour worked Monday in every cutoff 13-24: a control with no policy, a taxable 25.00 an hour premium (200.00 a cutoff) and a non-taxable one. The control's settlement is the Phase 24 control's, and the non-taxable worker's must equal it.

sources.bir: BIR RR 11-2018 as amended by TRAIN: semi-monthly withholding table effective 2023 onward (up to 10,417 exempt; 10,417 to 16,667: 15%; 16,667 to 33,333: 937.50 + 20%; over 33,333: 4,270.70 + 25% of the excess); annual table (up to 250,000 exempt; 250,000 to 400,000: 15% of the excess over 250,000). Only the employee's mandatory SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG contributions are excluded from taxable compensation (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(f)). Whether an employer-granted premium is taxable is the policy's own classification; the engine honours the rule's taxable flag.
sources.thirteenthMonth: Presidential Decree 851: 13th month pay = one twelfth of basic salary earned in the year; exempt up to 90,000 together with other benefits (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e)). A company premium is not basic salary and does not enter the 13th month.

assumptions: Tax year 2026, 24 semi-monthly cutoffs, 'split' timing, monthly salary 60,000 (30,000 a cutoff), every worker hired 2026-07-01 so only the 12 engine cutoffs 13-24 exist and there are no imported rows. An ordinary cutoff: gross 30,000; SSS 875, PhilHealth 750, Pag-IBIG 100 (1,725); taxable 28,275; withholding 937.50 + 0.20 x (28,275 - 16,667) = 3,259.10; net 25,015.90.

Every worker has one complete 09:00-18:00 punch with a 12:00-13:00 break (480 worked minutes) on a plain Monday in each cutoff, so the monthly salary is paid in full and the only difference between workers is the policy. The premium is a worked-time rule of 0 percent plus 25.00 an hour: 8 x 25.00 = 200.00 a cutoff, 2,400.00 over the 12 cutoffs. It is included in the SSS base and excluded from the Pag-IBIG base, and neither moves a contribution because 60,000 is already at the SSS and Pag-IBIG ceilings.

Year end for a worker with no 13th month paid: entries 12 x 30,000 plus the premiums; entitlement = basic earned 360,000 / 12 = 30,000 accrued unpaid and added to gross compensation; contributions 12 x 1,725 = 20,700; the 30,000 sits inside the 90,000 pool; non-taxable = pool + contributions + non-taxable premiums; taxable = gross - non-taxable; tax = 15% x (taxable - 250,000); withheld = the sum of the WHT lines only; a refund is a negative adjustment.

noPolicyControl.description: No pay policy. Gross 30,000, withholding 3,259.10 and net 25,015.90 in every cutoff. Year end: gross 390,000; non-taxable 50,700; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; withheld 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20.

taxablePremium.description: A taxable 25.00 an hour premium: 200.00 a cutoff. Cutoff gross 30,200, withholding 3,299.10, net 25,175.90. Year end: gross 360,000 + 2,400 + 30,000 = 392,400; non-taxable 50,700; taxable 341,700; tax 15% x 91,700 = 13,755.00; withheld 12 x 3,299.10 = 39,589.20; refund 25,834.20.

nonTaxablePremium.description: A non-taxable 25.00 an hour premium: 200.00 a cutoff. The cutoff withholds as if it were not paid: gross 30,200, withholding 3,259.10, net 25,215.90. Year end must exclude it too: gross 392,400; non-taxable 30,000 + 20,700 + 2,400 = 53,100; taxable 339,300; tax 13,395.00; withheld 39,109.20; refund 25,714.20, identical to the control. If year end taxed it the refund would be 360.00 too small.

limitations: Only the worked-time premium family (PREM-) is exercised, with a flat hourly amount. Holiday and rest-day (DAYPREM-), overtime (OTPREM-) and night differential (NDPREM-) premium lines reach the same year-end rule by code prefix and are not exercised separately.
Only an employee-scoped policy with one rule, one worked day per cutoff and a premium that is never limited. Percent-of-rate premiums, rate-table tiers and stacked policies are not exercised.
One salary, 'split' timing, a worker hired at the switch (no imported history), contributions at their ceilings.
Final pay (separation) derives year-to-date gross from released gross pay and is not exercised here; see Phase 25.
Year-end rows already computed under an older rule are replaced only when year end is recomputed.
